faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I'm getting a Reload Paper message. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The following can cause Reload Paper messages:
The paper may be loaded improperly (too far to the left) or roll paper has been loaded too far down into the printer. Roll paper should be lined up with the vertical and horizontal holes on the lower paper guide.
Measure the width of the media to make sure it exactly matches one of the supported paper widths (10", 24", 36", or 44"). A slight size variation (1/8" or 1/4") could cause a Reload Paper error.
Verify that there is no printed image or ink on either side of the media that can confuse the optical paper sensor.  Try loading a clean sheet of paper.
You may also get this message if using non-EPSON media, such as transparencies, velum, etc. Try loading EPSON media instead.
If none of these solutions work, there may be a physical problem with the printer. Please contact technical support at (888) 377-6611 or  (562) 276-1305 for assistance.

faqs.question: I see a communication error when I try to print. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following if you are getting a communication error when printing:
Make sure the type of driver you  installed matches the ink type in the printer.  Verify the ink type by checking the part number on the ink cartridges.
Make sure the printer interface setting matches the connection type you're using. By default, the printer interface should be set to Auto, which supports all connection types.
Check the physical cable connection and make sure the cable is not be longer than 10 ft. You may want to replace the cable.

faqs.question: How many prints can I print from an ink cartridge in my printer?
faqs.answer: There are too many variables to provide a count. You can estimate the amount by printing a Job Information sheet from the printer's Test Print menu. This sheet provides the amount of ink used for the last 10 print jobs, which can help you calculate ink usage.

faqs.question: My printer's ink cartridges are half full after I install the first set of ink cartridges. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer: Ink from the first set of ink cartridges is used to charge the printer's ink delivery system. This will not happen again when you install new ink cartridges.

faqs.question: How many cleaning cycles should I run to correct missing or deflected nozzles?
faqs.answer:
You should run up to eight cleaning cycles and print a nozzle check pattern between each one so the printer can perform a more extensive cleaning each time.
Note: Running cleaning cycles without printing a nozzle check between them causes the printer to use the same cleaning pressure level each time and may not clean all the nozzles thoroughly.

faqs.question: How frequently should I change the maintenance tank?
faqs.answer: You need to replace the maintenance tank only when the printer displays the "Maintenance Tank Almost Full" or "Maintenance Tank Full" message.

faqs.question: Why does my product advance the paper so much when set to roll cutter off?
faqs.answer: When the roll cutter off setting is selected, the printer advances the paper approximately eight inches in between each image or print job. This leaves enough room to cut between each image using scissors or the optional manual cutter.

faqs.question: What are the best settings to use with thicker media?
faqs.answer: If you are using EPSON media, just make sure you select the correct media type so your printer can set the appropriate Platen Gap setting (if Platen Gap is set to Auto in the SelectType menu).

faqs.question: Why does my product fail to cut paper when the Auto Cut setting is selected on my products control panel?
faqs.answer:
You may not have the auto cut option selected in the EPSON printer driver. Open the driver, click on the Paper tab, and select the auto cut setting if it is available.
Also make sure the media type setting is not too thick for the built-in cutter blade. It is recommended that you cut thicker media using scissors or the optional manual cutter.
The cutter blade may be dull from extensive use. Follow the instructions in the user manual to replace the cutter blade.

faqs.question: What types of paper can I use with the auto-cutter blade?
faqs.answer: You can use the auto-cutter blade with all EPSON media up to 11.5 mil thick. If the media you are using is thicker than 11.5 mil, it is strongly recommended that you do not use the "Roll Paper (Auto-Cut)" setting to avoid damaging the printer or the cutter blade (which is not covered under your warranty).

faqs.question: What does the 250 stand for in the Epson driver Media Type setting?
faqs.answer: The 250 designation represents the paper weight (250 gsm). Make sure you select the 250 Media Type setting if the media installed in the printer is 250 gsm (roll paper). If there is a mismatch in paper weight, print quality may be affected by horizontal banding or other problems.

faqs.answer: If fonts and images print with jagged edges the resolution of the file may be too low to print smoothly, or the file may contain PostScript data. You may need to purchase RIP (Raster Image Processing) hardware or software.

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The most common cause of vertical banding is over-saturation of the media, usually created by paper "rippling".  To correct this effect, decrease the saturation and lower the paper suction. If vertical banding is still apparent print the image with high speed off (uni-directional).  If this corrects the issue, align the print head, as described on page 5-6 of the Users Guide.

faqs.question: There are vertical bands or lines on my printout.  What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Run three auto print head alignments.
Make sure High Speed is not selected.
Lower the dpi setting you selected to print.  If you selected 2880 dpi, lower                     the setting to 1440 dpi.
Make sure the lines are not in the image source.
Make sure you use the correct profile settings.

faqs.answer: Print a nozzle check pattern. If you see gaps in the nozzle check pattern, run three cleaning cycles, then print another nozzle check pattern to see if all nozzles print now. If you still see gaps, run a power cleaning cycle.

faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I see horizontal or vertical lines in my printout. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Perform a nozzle check from the printer's control panel or the Epson printer driver, then do one of the following:
If there are gaps in the nozzle check pattern, clean the print head nozzles.
If there are no gaps in the nozzle check pattern, try the solutions below.
Horizontal Banding
Increase the print resolution.
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Select an alternate paper profile for ink coverage.
Select the correct paper type in the printer driver.
Adjust the paper feed
Vertical Banding
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Align the print head.

faqs.question: What are the best driver settings to use with my paper type?
faqs.answer: The SP7600/9600 driver lists most (if not all) EPSON media types. If your media type is not listed, see the documentation that came with the media. If you're using non-Epson media, please contact your vendor and ensure that the media is compatible with your printer and which driver setting will give the best results.

faqs.question: Do I need the Fiery Spark Pro 2.0 RIP for my photographic workflow?
faqs.answer: If all your work is produced as RGB, then the Fiery Spark Pro 2.0 is not necessary since the EPSON Standard Photographic printer driver should be sufficient to do the job. However, if you place your images into a page layout application such as Quark Xpress, In Design, Illustrator, or PageMaker and use PostScript fonts, then you may want to consider using the RIP.

faqs.question: Why have my pre-defined paper settings changed?
faqs.answer: If you name a custom paper setting using the same name as a pre-defined paper (like A4), the pre-defined paper settings are over written by the custom settings.

faqs.question: How should my product be prepared for shipment and storage?
faqs.answer:
If you are transporting the printer only a short distance in a horizontal position, or if you are going to store it for less than 6 months, you don't need to perform the ink draining process described on page 5-25 of the User's Guide. Instead, follow the instructions below:
Remove any paper and the paper spindle from the printer. Power off the printer from the control panel.
Wait until the print head moves to the home position in the far right corner and the LCD display turns off.
Install the metal shipping bracket to secure the print head in place. If you do not have the shipping bracket, contact EPSON technical support or your dealer to request one. Make sure the head is locked in place securely so it won't slide out of home position.
Remove the power cord from the back of the printer. Remove the ink cartridges from the ink housing and close the ink housing cover door. Tape all the covers closed so they don't open during transport.
If your printer is installed on the optional stand, remove the printer from the stand.
If you have the original shipping crate, place the printer in the crate with proper packing materials. If you do not have the original shipping crate, take extra care when packing the printer to prevent it from sustaining any shipping damage. Shipping damage caused by improper packing is not covered under warranty.
Do not ship the ink cartridges inside the printer crate. Place the ink cartridges inside a plastic bag and ship them separately to prevent ink spills.

faqs.question: What are the recommended cut methods for No Margin borderless printing?
faqs.answer: For "borderless" printing, you may choose the 1CUT or 2CUT method. The 1CUT method cuts edge-to-edge and occasionally may crop your images when cutting between them. The 2CUT method is recommended for optimal no margin prints.

faqs.question: Why can't I service my product myself?
faqs.answer: EPSON has made some items user-replaceable on the Stylus Pro 7600/9600, however some of the components require precision adjustments that can only be performed by a trained service technician.

faqs.question: What are the user replaceable parts for the 9600 and 7600?
faqs.answer: The ink cartridges, cutter blade, and maintenance tank.
